key_insight: A 13-feature, interpretable model mined from discharge reports can identify cardiovascular patients at higher 24-month atrial fibrillation risk better than common clinical risk scores.
clinical_relevance: This could help hospitals flag higher-risk patients using routinely collected EHR data, supporting earlier monitoring and follow-up in a high-risk cardiovascular population.
method: Retrospective single-center study of adults with cardiovascular disease and no prior atrial fibrillation.
Custom NLP turned discharge reports into 73 structured features; LightAutoML built full, simple, and linear risk-score models.
Performance was compared with CHARGE-AF, C2HEST, MHS, and HAVOC and interpreted with SHAP.
evidence_signal: Among 17,562 eligible patients, 1,438 developed AF; the simple model (Pre-AF 13) achieved ROC AUC 0.725 at 24 months and 0.696 over full follow-up, outperforming the benchmark clinical scores.
watch_item: Single-center retrospective data may limit generalizability, and external validation is needed before routine implementation.
paper_title: Pre-AF 13: An Interpretable Atrial Fibrillation Risk Score Mined from Discharge Reports
